questions.q: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team found that, among P2T calls that pass the artifact filter, a sizeable group has high TXR1 copy number and/or a low junction alt allele fraction, and treated these as a separate group when deciding who has SV-driven target-mediated activation. Your notes say you checked purity/copy-adjusted alt fraction, but your stated target definition uses only artifact flags, ASE and phase. Check in your data how copy number and purity-adjusted junction allele fraction are distributed among your target cases, and whether cases with amplification or a subclonal junction behave like the rest of your target. Does that change who belongs in your target population?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: you reported that your doubly robust estimate was unstable (low control effective sample size, a very large maximum combined weight) and that your result depends on the estimator. The other team did not record that instability in its target population. Check where your extreme weights come from: which patients carry them, whether they come from the treatment model or the assessment model, and whether they concentrate in a subgroup of your target that could be defined by tumour-genomic features. Does what you find change your target definition or your choice of primary estimator?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team found that a small number of target cases have a low-confidence DLR1 call and checked whether excluding them moved the toxicity risk and the benefit estimate. Your records show no check of DLR1 call confidence. Check whether low-confidence calls exist in your target and whether the activity score is reliable for them. Does it change how you standardize the toxicity risk?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team flagged artifact-prone P2T calls using segmental-duplication overlap together with breakpoint homology length and low-complexity fraction, and arrived at a somewhat different count of excluded calls than your segdup-plus-MAPQ rule. Check which P2T calls the two kinds of rule would classify differently in your data and whether those calls look like true junctions. Does it change your artifact filter?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team found that its doubly robust estimate of the benefit difference was unstable: the product of treatment and assessment weights gave a low effective sample size in the comparator arm and a very large maximum weight, and the point estimate differed noticeably from its bootstrap median and from outcome-model standardization. You clipped assessment probabilities at a floor. Check in your target the effective sample size per arm, the maximum combined weight, how many patients hit the clip, and how far your estimate moves with no clipping, with other clip levels, and with pure outcome-model standardization. Does it change which estimator you treat as primary?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team defined the target population without a copy-number or junction-clonality requirement, using artifact flags plus ASE and phase support, and chose its cut-offs from the bimodal distributions of the molecular features alone. You wrote that your thresholds were informed partly by naive outcome patterns within strata. Check whether your copy-number and alt-fraction cut-offs can be justified from the molecular data alone (for example after adjusting allele fraction for purity and local copy number), without looking at benefit by stratum, and whether amplified or low-allele-fraction cases that still show haplotype-linked expression are really not SV-driven target-mediated activation. Does it change who belongs in your target population?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team checked treatment positivity within site-by-period cells and weighted standardized mean differences after adjustment, and recorded that confounded treatment assignment and purity/copy distortion of allele fractions were both present in the data and changed its method. Your records show a propensity range and batch balance only. Check positivity by site and calendar period and covariate balance after weighting inside your target, and whether your raw alt-fraction cut-off is distorted by tumour purity or copy number. Does it change your confounder set or your target criteria?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team standardized the TXR1i toxicity risk over the whole target population (both arms) with the DLR1 activity score entered as a categorical variable, because the toxicity rate changed sharply and non-linearly across score levels. Check how you coded the activity score, whether a linear term fits the observed toxicity by score level in your data, and over which patients you averaged the predicted TXR1i toxicity. Does it change your toxicity estimate's method?

referee.difference: Both teams use the same estimands and similar estimators (AIPW/g-computation, MAR given covariates, arm and 8-week toxicity; toxicity standardized over the target under TXR1i), and their toxicity risks are close (33.5 vs 34.9). The difference is the rows kept, i.e. how 'SV-driven TXR1 target-mediated activation' is read. X's target (n=481) is a strict subset of Y's (n=666). X also requires a clonal junction (purity/copy-corrected CCF>=0.55), no high-level gain (local copy<=3.6) and stricter ASE/phase cut-offs. Y keeps the 185 extra P2T cases, which are mostly high-copy (median 5.3) with a subclonal junction (median CCF 0.30). Including them lowers the benefit RD from about 29 to about 17pp.
referee.test: work/test1.py: fit TXR1 expression on copy, lineage marker, purity and batch in NONE-topology cases, then compare residual expression in the core (X and Y) group and the disputed (Y-only) group. work/test2.py: within each group, separately estimate the adjusted week-16 benefit RD (g-computation integrating over an arm-specific 8-week toxicity model, all-assessed hypothetical estimand) with a 150-rep bootstrap, plus the standardized TXR1i toxicity.
referee.reason: The disputed cases show no TXR1i benefit, and the CI excludes the core effect. Their junction is subclonal or amplified and their expression excess is only partial. So Y's broader target mixes in a non-responsive, non-target-mediated subgroup that dilutes the estimand. Both teams agree on the toxicity component and on code 1, so the dispute is the benefit size: X's 29.1pp and net 17.4pp are supported. Caveat: the test uses outcomes to arbitrate a target definition. X's cut-offs were set on molecular grounds (a bimodal CCF gap), and the expression test, which is outcome-free, points the same way.

shared_assumptions: Both teams flipped the chr3 haplotype labels so that h1 minus h2 A-fraction has the same sign on all four chromosomes. Both selection rules (sign consistency / maximum separation, and maximum two-state Markov likelihood over 8 groupings) reward between-parent separation in A-fraction, so they are not independent confirmations of each other. Neither team calibrated the rule against a null in which the two parents have similar fractions and the labels as given are correct, with only four chromosomes.

Both teams use the same estimator form, t = switches / (2 m (1-m) L) (team B's L_A(1-m) + L_B m is algebraically the same), with m set to that haplotype's own observed A-fraction. Neither tested how t moves if m is a population/source proportion rather than the single haplotype's realised fraction, nor whether the rate is t or t-1 generations of recombination.

Both teams removed the eight 0.03 M low-posterior segments from the span (denominator) rather than keeping the span and assigning it the ancestry of the merged flanks. Neither reports how much the A-fractions and t change under the other treatment.

Both teams treat the two haplotypes as independent Poisson/Markov switch processes after masking; the exactly mirrored artefacts and the near-coincident chr1 breakpoints show that h1 and h2 calls are not fully independent.
Both assume a single shared t convention applies per parent and that one pulse fits each parent; neither tested tract-length distribution fit (exponential) within each parent.
unused_evidence: map_info.tsv.gz (chromosome genetic lengths 2.8, 2.8, 3.1, 2.9 M): team A compared it with the called span; team B's notes do not mention it. The uncalled chromosome ends (for example 0.03 M at the start and 0.08 M at the end of chr1) are neither in the span nor in the exposure, and neither team says whether the first and last tracts were treated as censored at the called boundary or at the chromosome end.

Gap coordinates as a signal: the 12 uncalled gaps were used only as 'one switch each'. Neither team tabulated whether gaps on h1 and h2 fall at the same positions (for example chr1 h1 gap 1.4788-1.5037 and chr1 h2 gap 1.4854-1.5132 overlap, at the site team B flagged as a possible phase switch). Overlapping gaps on both haplotypes would point to a phase-switch or shared breakpoint artefact rather than two independent ancestry switches.

Switch density per chromosome and haplotype, separately from A-fraction, as an independent discriminator of which chr3 haplotype belongs with which parent. Team B's likelihood mixes it with A-fraction; team A did not use it.
posterior and low_complexity_frac take only two value pairs (0.985/0.08 and 0.62/0.92), so they were used fully as a mask; no further information there.
unresolved_weak_points: Team A: the chr3 swap is 'inferred from separation and sign consistency, which can bias the difference upward'; the unphased check 'agrees roughly' (0.34/0.71) but the size of the upward bias was never estimated. Reported, not resolved.
Team B: the assignment likelihood is 'partly inflated by choosing among 8 groupings' and dLL of 3.55-4.6 was not compared with a null distribution. Reported, not resolved.

Team B: the chr1 possible phase switch near 1.49 M was kept as given although the stated sensitivity (0.25/4.4 and 0.80/6.3) moves all four reported numbers. Team A found coincident opposite breakpoints and did not change the method either. Reported, not resolved.
Both: t rests on 16 and 26 switches with wide intervals, and team B says its t convention may differ from another by about 1 generation. Neither tested which convention the data support.
second_readings: 'the called tract span': (a) sum of called segment lengths after removing artefacts (what both did), (b) sum of all called segment lengths including the eight low-confidence segments reassigned to flank ancestry, or (c) first-to-last called coordinate including interior gaps. These change the denominators of both the fraction and t.

'each transmitted parental haplotype': read literally the file's h1 and h2 are the two transmitted haplotypes as phased; the teams instead rebuilt parents by flipping chr3. If the phasing is trio-based or otherwise genome-wide consistent, the as-given pooled fractions (about 0.565 and 0.482) and their t values are the answer, and chr3 is simply a chromosome where the lower-A parent transmitted a high-A haplotype.

'number of generations since a single recent admixture pulse' per parent: the per-haplotype m in the switch-rate formula versus one admixture proportion for the pulse; and whether t counts meioses on the transmitted haplotype (parent's t plus one) or generations before the parent.
'fraction of ancestry A': Morgan-weighted (both teams) versus any other weighting; only Morgans are given, so this reading is settled.
challenge.verdict: Moderate trust at best: the two teams agree, but both reach the answer through the same chr3 label flip chosen by a separation-maximising rule on only four chromosomes, and neither calibrated it against chance or resolved the chr1 phase-switch sensitivity that moves all four numbers. The fractions and t values should not go out until the flip is tested with evidence independent of A-fraction and the span and gap treatments are shown not to matter.

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: You said your t convention may differ from another by about 1 generation, and your exposure excludes gap length while each gap still contributes a switch. Recompute t for each parent (a) with gap length added back to the exposure, (b) with the artefact span kept and assigned flank ancestry, and (c) from A tracts alone and from B tracts alone using map_info chromosome ends to decide which boundary tracts are censored. referee.difference: Both teams mask the same 8 artefact segments, flip chr3 between parents, and use the same switch-rate estimator. The main difference is that Y treats the overlapping opposite-direction gaps on chr1 (h1 A->B gap 1.4788-1.5037 M, h2 B->A gap 1.4854-1.5132 M) as a within-chromosome phase-switch error. Y swaps the haplotypes distal to 1.49 M, which removes 2 switches and moves the answer from 0.301/0.747 to 0.250/0.797, and parent1 t from about 3.4 to 4.43. X does not correct it. A minor second difference is that X puts interior gap length in the switch exposure (11.15 M vs about 10.85 M), which changes t by about 3%.
referee.test: test_phase.py: simulate the null of no phase error. The two parental haplotypes on each chromosome are independent two-state Markov single-pulse tracts with X's fitted m and t (0.301/3.41, 0.747/6.16), over the observed called spans, with random chromosome-to-parent assignment. Each breakpoint gets an uncalled gap with the observed frequency (12/42) and an observed width. 20000 replicates. Two statistics compared with the data: (1) the minimum distance between opposite-direction switches on h1 and h2 of the same chromosome (observed 0.0080 M, gap midpoints); (2) at least one overlapping opposite-direction gap pair (observed 1).
referee.reason: Y's chr1 swap is a data edit that changes both A-fractions by 0.05 and parent1 t by 1 generation. The test shows the evidence for it (the coincident opposite switches) is what independent real recombinations produce routinely (P 0.09-0.26). Without that edit Y's estimates reduce to X's (0.301/3.50, 0.747/6.34). The remaining gap-exposure difference is small, and X's choice is the better justified one: each gap brackets a breakpoint, so gap length belongs in the exposure over which switches can occur.

sl-dev-v2-local-21520857ea5a.label: Purity/copy-number confound allelic evidence
sl-dev-v2-local-21520857ea5a.text: PITFALL: Raw allele fractions (alt_molecule_fraction, target_ase_alt_fraction) are diluted by low tumor purity and distorted by local copy-number gain or WGD, so a true clonal SV in a low-purity sample can look weak, and amplification can raise TXR1 or mimic allelic imbalance without any SV. CHECK: Plot alt_molecule_fraction and ASE fraction against tumor_purity, local_total_copy, tumor_ploidy and wgd_flag; check whether high TXR1 expression in non-P2T cases tracks local_total_copy. IF FOUND: Purity/copy-adjust the fractions (expected fraction about purity*mutant copies/total copies) before applying any threshold, so that low-purity true SVs are not excluded; do not count amplification-only activation as SV-driven. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7985293/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6778654/.

sl-dev-v2-local-87d7b79f8c08.label: Missing week-16 outcome: hypothetical estimand
sl-dev-v2-local-87d7b79f8c08.text: PITFALL: A complete-case analysis of week-16 benefit (dropping assessed16==0) is biased when non-assessment depends on prognosis or on treatment toxicity; early toxicity discontinuation is a likely cause of missing week-16 visits under TXR1i. CHECK: Tabulate assessed16 by therapy_class, tox_stop_8wk, ecog, tumor_burden, site and calendar_period; fit a model for P(assessed16=1 | treatment, baseline covariates). IF FOUND: The estimand 'as if all had an assessable week-16 visit' is a hypothetical estimand: estimate it with inverse-probability-of-missingness weights multiplied by treatment weights, or with g-computation/AIPW (doubly robust), under MAR given the covariates; state that this assumption cannot be tested and run a sensitivity analysis (delta/tipping-point). Do not impute non-assessed as failure, which is a composite estimand and not the one asked for. SOURCE: https://database.ich.org/sites/default/files/E9%2DR1_Step4_Guideline_2019_1203.pdf ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10228513/.

sl-dev-v2-local-d6dc78fa4f1a.label: Confounding and positivity diagnostics
sl-dev-v2-local-d6dc78fa4f1a.text: PITFALL: Registry treatment choice is confounded (ECOG, tumor burden, prior lines/resistance, lineage, site, calendar period), and in the target population nearly everyone may have received TXR1i, so IPW gives extreme weights or the comparison is unsupported by data. CHECK: Within the target population, check propensity score overlap by arm, max/min weights, effective sample size and weighted standardized mean differences (<0.1) for all baseline confounders; look for structural non-positivity (e.g. a site or period with no SYS patients). IF FOUND: Use a doubly robust estimator, report the region with overlap, and say explicitly if trimming or overlap weights move the estimand away from the full target population; never trim silently. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8492528/ ; https://academic.oup.com/aje/article/188/1/250/5090958.

sl-dev-v2-local-3a34f6061005.label: Target trial alignment at time zero
sl-dev-v2-local-3a34f6061005.text: PITFALL: Restricting to outside analysis_set, or using covariates or outcomes measured after treatment start, breaks the target trial: eligibility, assignment and time zero must line up, or selection and immortal-time bias follow. Adjusting for post-baseline variables such as assessed16 or toxicity opens collider bias. CHECK: Use only analysis_set==1 as the time-zero cohort; check time_zero_day and that every covariate is baseline; never put tox_stop_8wk into the treatment or benefit confounder set. IF FOUND: Keep only baseline confounders in the treatment model; handle post-baseline events through the missingness model, not through eligibility. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5124536/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12927355/.

sl-dev-v2-local-93613e74c9f8.label: DLR1 activity score and marginal toxicity
sl-dev-v2-local-93613e74c9f8.text: PITFALL: Toxicity under TXR1i probably depends on germline DLR1 metabolizer status; treating each star allele as a separate category, or ignoring low-confidence diplotype calls, misrepresents that risk. Because the requested toxicity risk is a marginal risk under TXR1i in the whole target population, a crude rate among TXR1i-treated patients is biased if their DLR1 or clinical makeup differs from the whole target population. CHECK: Compute activity score = sum of the two haplotype activity values from dlr1_allele_table; tabulate tox_stop_8wk by activity score under TXR1i; check dlr1_call_confidence and ancestry_group. IF FOUND: Estimate the 8-week toxicity risk under TXR1i by standardizing (g-computation or IPW) over the whole target population's covariate distribution, including activity score; handle low-confidence calls through a sensitivity analysis or multiple imputation. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6951851/ ; https://pharmcat.clinpgx.org/methods/Matching-Recommendations/.

sl-dev-v2-local-e2a9a83f433e.label: Batch/lineage and subgroup misclassification
sl-dev-v2-local-e2a9a83f433e.text: PITFALL: Expression features (txr1_log_tpm, ASE) can be shifted by expression_batch, rna_quality and library size, and TXR1 baseline expression correlates with the lineage program, so fixed expression cut-offs misclassify cases; misclassifying who belongs to the biomarker subgroup biases the subgroup effect toward the effect in the misclassified group, usually toward the null. CHECK: Compare txr1_log_tpm and housekeeping_log_tpm across expression_batch and rna_quality; regress TXR1 on lineage_marker_log_tpm to obtain lineage-adjusted residual expression; check how stable subgroup membership is under alternative definitions. IF FOUND: Normalize within batch and use lineage-adjusted expression only as supporting evidence; report effect estimates under the stricter and the looser definitions of the subgroup. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4107031/ ; https://doi.org/10.1111/rssc.12364.

sl-dev-v2-local-31a9a7a08b39.label: Marginal RD in target population
sl-dev-v2-local-31a9a7a08b39.text: PITFALL: The TXR1i benefit is likely concentrated in true SV-driven tumors (effect modification), so an estimate over the full registry, or one conditional on covariates (such as a logistic odds ratio), is not the requested marginal risk difference in the target population. CHECK: Estimate the effect in the target group and in non-target groups separately; make sure the reported number is a standardized marginal risk difference in percentage points. IF FOUND: Fit the models within the target population, or include interactions, and marginalize over the target population's covariates; use bootstrap CIs that repeat the whole pipeline (missingness weights, propensity, outcome, toxicity) and propagate uncertainty into net utility = RD - 0.35*toxicity risk. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4052139/.

sl-dev-v2-local-dff9f74f2f47.label: Tract-length rate is t(1-m), not t
sl-dev-v2-local-dff9f74f2f47.text: PITFALL: Using t = 1/(mean tract length) ignores invisible within-ancestry recombination; under a single pulse t generations ago with ancestry-A fraction m, tracts of ancestry A are exponential with rate t*(1-m) per Morgan (not t), and B tracts with rate t*m, so the naive estimator is biased by a factor 1/(1-m) and badly wrong when m is far from 0.5. CHECK: estimate t separately from A tracts and from B tracts on the same haplotype using rate=t*(1-m) and rate=t*m; the two must agree, and compare against the naive 1/mean which will not. IF FOUND: estimate t jointly, e.g. t = S / (2*m*(1-m)*L) where S is the number of observed ancestry switches and L the total called span in Morgans, or equivalently t = 1/(mean_A_length*(1-m)). SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.05904 and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3374321/

sl-dev-v2-local-3df09f4e7b3f.label: Censoring at chromosome and span ends
sl-dev-v2-local-3df09f4e7b3f.text: PITFALL: Tracts that touch the start or end of a chromosome or of the called span are right-censored (truncated), so treating their observed length as a complete tract shortens the mean and inflates t. CHECK: per chromosome and haplotype, count how many segments begin at the first called coordinate or end at the last called coordinate, and what fraction of total A span they hold; compare mean length of boundary versus interior tracts. IF FOUND: use the censored exponential MLE, rate = (number of uncensored tract ends) / (total Morgan span of all tracts of that ancestry, censored ones included in the denominator); equivalently count ancestry switches as events and total span as exposure. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8557420/ and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3374321/

sl-dev-v2-local-87640e8f459f.label: Spurious short low-confidence segments
sl-dev-v2-local-87640e8f459f.text: PITFALL: Spurious very short segments from local-ancestry inference error (low posterior, repeat or low-complexity regions) add fake ancestry switches, inflate t, and make a non-exponential length distribution look exponential. CHECK: tabulate segment length against the posterior and low_complexity_frac columns and look for an excess of segments below about 1-2 cM concentrated at low posterior or high low_complexity_frac. IF FOUND: drop segments failing a posterior threshold (for example below 0.9) or with high low_complexity_frac (for example above 0.5), remove their span from the denominator rather than counting them as switches, and report how sensitive t is to the threshold. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3374321/ and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9943733/

sl-dev-v2-local-faede5184b44.label: Merge adjacent same-ancestry tracts
sl-dev-v2-local-faede5184b44.text: PITFALL: After filtering or across gaps, adjacent segments of the same ancestry left unmerged are counted as two tracts separated by a switch, which roughly doubles the inferred switch rate. CHECK: scan the segment list per chromosome and haplotype for consecutive rows carrying the same anc label, and for same-ancestry pairs that flank a dropped or uncalled interval. IF FOUND: merge them into one tract, summing length and excluding any uncalled interval from the span, before any likelihood or mean-length calculation. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3374321/

sl-dev-v2-local-ffdbe7b69527.label: Interchromosomal phase: h1/h2 may not be one parent
sl-dev-v2-local-ffdbe7b69527.text: PITFALL: Haplotype labels h1 and h2 are assigned independently per chromosome, so they need not correspond to the same parent genome-wide (interchromosomal phase ambiguity); pooling chromosomes under mislabelled haplotypes pulls both parental A-fractions toward the genome-wide mean and shortens apparent tracts, so the parental difference is understated and t overstated. CHECK: compute the per-chromosome A-fraction for h1 minus h2 and see whether the sign is consistent across chromosomes; inconsistent signs with large magnitudes indicate label swapping, whereas a consistent sign supports genome-wide-consistent labels. IF FOUND: resolve labels per chromosome (for example by assigning each chromosome's haplotypes so as to maximise the between-haplotype A-fraction separation), note that this choice biases the estimated difference upward, and cross-check with an unphased, homozygosity-based estimate of the two parental fractions. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9388397/ and https://doi.org/10.1093/g3journal/jkaf122

sl-dev-v2-local-f54ae62b10be.label: Switch errors appear as coincident breakpoints
sl-dev-v2-local-f54ae62b10be.text: PITFALL: A phasing switch error inside a chromosome looks exactly like a real ancestry switch and appears as two coincident, opposite ancestry breakpoints on h1 and h2 at the same coordinate, which inflates the switch count on both haplotypes and biases t upward while mixing the two parents' ancestry fractions. CHECK: list breakpoint coordinates for h1 and h2 per chromosome and flag positions where both haplotypes switch at the same Morgan coordinate in opposite directions (A-to-B on one, B-to-A on the other). IF FOUND: treat it as a phase error, flip the downstream haplotype assignment to restore the longer tracts, and recompute; if the pattern is frequent, prefer a phase-free or unphased estimator of the parental fractions and times. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1093/g3journal/jkaf122 and https://doi.org/10.1002/cpz1.70321

sl-dev-v2-local-e5ee3790a7a0.label: Length-weighted fraction over called span only
sl-dev-v2-local-e5ee3790a7a0.text: PITFALL: The ancestry-A fraction must be Morgan-length-weighted over the span actually called, not a count of segments and not a physical-position or whole-chromosome denominator; the called tract span can be shorter than the chromosome lengths given in map_info.tsv, and using chromosome length as the denominator deflates both fractions. CHECK: for each haplotype sum the segment lengths per chromosome and compare with length_morgan in map_info.tsv to quantify uncalled flanks and interior gaps; verify the two haplotypes cover the same span. IF FOUND: set the denominator to the sum of retained, called segment lengths in Morgans per haplotype, and use the same span consistently for the fraction and for the exposure in the rate estimate. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3374321/

sl-dev-v2-local-ac176d066086.label: Few tracts: high variance and downward bias in t
sl-dev-v2-local-ac176d066086.text: PITFALL: With one individual's genome there are few tracts, so the time estimate has a large variance and a known downward bias, and for very recent admixture (small t) tract lengths are neither exponential nor independent because the pedigree and within-ancestry recombination dominate. CHECK: count uncensored tracts per haplotype; if fewer than about 20, compute a confidence interval for the rate (a Poisson interval on the switch count divided by exposure) and also derive t separately from the A tracts, the B tracts, and the pooled switch rate to see if they agree. IF FOUND: report t from the pooled switch-rate estimator rather than from one ancestry's mean length, state the interval, and do not over-round a point estimate that the data cannot support. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4096373/ and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9388397/

sl-dev-v2-local-00914fff025e.label: Generation-counting convention off by one
sl-dev-v2-local-00914fff025e.text: PITFALL: The generation convention is ambiguous and can shift the answer by a whole generation: a haplotype transmitted to the focal individual has passed through one meiosis per generation since the pulse, including the meiosis that produced the focal individual, so an estimate of recombination-rate-per-Morgan equals the number of meioses, not necessarily the number of generations as the grader defines it. CHECK: state explicitly which convention is used, and test both (t and t-1 or t+1) against the observed mean tract length to see which is consistent with the ancestry fractions. IF FOUND: adopt the convention in which tracts of ancestry A are exponential with rate t*(1-m) where t is generations since the admixture pulse for that parental haplotype, and say so in the reasoning so the number is interpretable. SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.05904 and https://web.stanford.edu/group/pritchardlab/HGbook/ReleaseV1.1/HGBook-V1.1-ch3.2.pdf

sl-dev-v2-local-a9cc7c023070.label: Estimate per haplotype; label parents last
sl-dev-v2-local-a9cc7c023070.text: PITFALL: Forcing the two haplotypes to share one admixture time, or pooling both haplotypes' tracts into one likelihood, hides genuinely different parental histories, which is exactly what the task asks to resolve; conversely, labelling parent1 and parent2 before the QC filters are applied can swap the labels because filtering changes each haplotype's A-fraction. CHECK: fit the A-fraction and t independently for each haplotype, then compare the two times and fractions; recompute the A-fractions after every filtering decision and see whether the ordering of the two haplotypes ever changes. IF FOUND: keep per-haplotype estimates, and assign parent1 as the smaller final A-fraction only after all QC is settled, reporting the gap between the two fractions so a near-tie is visible. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9388397/ and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7449501/

sl-dev-v2-local-663c5be4f2c9.reason: The target population definition decides which patients enter every estimate; a wrong definition changes all four reported numbers.
sl-dev-v2-local-663c5be4f2c9.text: Who counts as 'SV-driven TXR1 target-mediated activation' has to be decided from the data, not read off one column. High TXR1 expression alone, or the mere presence of a reported junction, mixes in non-driving SVs and lineage-driven high expression: most SVs near a gene do not change its expression, and only promoter-facing enhancer-hijack rearrangements activate it. Check: cross-tabulate breakpoint_topology (P2T versus INV/D2T/NONE) against txr1_log_tpm, lineage_marker_log_tpm, target_ase_alt_fraction and phase_consistency, and see whether high-TXR1 cases without P2T are explained by lineage expression or copy number. If so, define the target population from mechanism-consistent evidence across modalities (P2T topology plus adequate alt_molecule_fraction plus haplotype-consistent ASE/phase), and report how the estimates move under alternative definitions.

sl-dev-v2-local-996bb40ad9ff.reason: False-positive SV calls would put non-target tumors into the target population and dilute the effect estimate.
sl-dev-v2-local-996bb40ad9ff.text: Some reported P2T junctions may be artifacts. Long-read SV calls at loci with segmental duplication, high homology or low complexity are often false positives from mis-mapping to paralogous copies. Check: among P2T calls, by platform, look at mapq_median, segmental_dup_overlap, homology_bp, low_complexity_score, split_molecule_count, molecule_depth and read_n50; flag P2T calls with low MAPQ or high segmental-duplication overlap that also lack expression, ASE or phase support. If found: treat artifact-prone calls as not SV-driven, or as uncertain with sensitivity analyses that include and exclude them, instead of trusting the topology label.

sl-dev-v2-local-3e5644dfaced.reason: A fixed raw-fraction threshold would wrongly exclude low-purity true SV cases and could admit amplification-only cases, shifting target membership.
sl-dev-v2-local-3e5644dfaced.text: Raw allele fractions (alt_molecule_fraction, target_ase_alt_fraction) are diluted by low tumor purity and distorted by local copy-number gain or whole-genome doubling. A true clonal SV in a low-purity sample can look weak, and amplification can raise TXR1 expression or mimic allelic imbalance with no SV. Check: plot alt_molecule_fraction and the ASE fraction against tumor_purity, local_total_copy, tumor_ploidy and wgd_flag; check whether high TXR1 expression in non-P2T cases tracks local_total_copy. If found: adjust the fractions for purity and copy number (expected fraction is roughly purity x mutant copies / total copies) before applying any threshold, so low-purity true SVs are not excluded; do not count amplification-only activation as SV-driven.

sl-dev-v2-local-477eabcc064a.reason: Batch and lineage effects on expression could misclassify who is in the target population if expression is used as evidence.
sl-dev-v2-local-477eabcc064a.text: Expression features (txr1_log_tpm, ASE) can be shifted by expression_batch, rna_quality and library size, and baseline TXR1 expression correlates with the lineage program, so fixed expression cut-offs misclassify cases. Misclassified subgroup membership biases the subgroup effect toward the effect in the misclassified group, usually toward the null. Check: compare txr1_log_tpm and housekeeping_log_tpm across expression_batch and rna_quality; regress TXR1 on lineage_marker_log_tpm to get lineage-adjusted residual expression; check how stable subgroup membership is under alternative definitions. If found: normalize within batch, use lineage-adjusted expression only as supporting evidence, and report effect estimates under a stricter and a looser subgroup definition.

sl-dev-v2-local-caee1f4d19e0.reason: Choosing the wrong cohort or adjusting for post-treatment variables biases the benefit estimate.
sl-dev-v2-local-caee1f4d19e0.text: Keep eligibility, treatment assignment and time zero aligned. Use only analysis_set==1 as the time-zero cohort, check time_zero_day, and confirm every covariate used for adjustment is measured at baseline. Post-baseline variables such as assessed16 and tox_stop_8wk must never go into the treatment (confounder) model or be used to restrict the cohort: that causes selection, immortal-time and collider bias. Post-baseline events are handled through the missingness model, not through eligibility.

sl-dev-v2-local-fad17919d094.reason: A crude arm comparison is confounded, and poor overlap can make a weighted estimate unstable or change the population it refers to.
sl-dev-v2-local-fad17919d094.text: Treatment choice in the registry is not random: it is likely confounded by ECOG, tumor burden, prior lines/resistance, lineage, site and calendar period. Within the target population nearly everyone may have received TXR1i, so inverse-probability weights can become extreme or the comparison may lack data support. Check, within the target population: propensity-score overlap by arm, maximum/minimum weights, effective sample size, weighted standardized mean differences (aim below 0.1) for all baseline confounders, and structural non-positivity (for example a site or period with no non-TXR1 systemic-therapy patients). If found: use a doubly robust estimator, report the region with overlap, and say explicitly if trimming or overlap weights move the estimand away from the full target population; never trim silently.

sl-dev-v2-local-136ee75d0dea.reason: How missing week-16 outcomes are handled determines whether the estimate matches the estimand the task names.
sl-dev-v2-local-136ee75d0dea.text: The benefit estimand 'as if all patients had an assessable week-16 visit' is a hypothetical estimand. A complete-case analysis that drops assessed16==0 is biased if non-assessment depends on prognosis or on treatment toxicity; early toxicity discontinuation is a likely cause of missing week-16 visits under TXR1i. Check: tabulate assessed16 by therapy_class, tox_stop_8wk, ecog, tumor_burden, site and calendar_period, and fit a model for P(assessed16=1 | treatment, baseline covariates). If non-assessment is non-random: use inverse-probability-of-missingness weights multiplied by the treatment weights, or g-computation/AIPW, under missing-at-random given covariates; state that this assumption cannot be tested and run a delta/tipping-point sensitivity analysis. Do not impute non-assessed patients as failures: that answers a composite estimand, not the one asked for.

sl-dev-v2-local-adfe08ff492c.reason: Reporting a pooled or conditional effect instead of the target-population marginal risk difference gives the wrong quantity.
sl-dev-v2-local-adfe08ff492c.text: The requested benefit number is a standardized marginal risk difference in percentage points within the target population. TXR1i benefit is likely concentrated in true SV-driven tumors (effect modification), so an estimate over the whole registry, or a conditional measure such as a logistic-regression odds ratio or coefficient, is not what is asked. Check by estimating the effect separately in target and non-target groups. Fit the models within the target population, or with treatment-by-target interactions, and marginalize over the target population's covariate distribution. Bootstrap the whole pipeline (missingness weights, propensity, outcome and toxicity models) for confidence intervals and carry the uncertainty into net utility = benefit RD - 0.35 x toxicity risk.

sl-dev-v2-local-496b3750c020.reason: The toxicity term enters net utility directly; a crude treated-only rate or mishandled pharmacogene coding would misstate it.
sl-dev-v2-local-496b3750c020.text: The 8-week toxicity/discontinuation risk asked for is a marginal risk under TXR1i over the whole target population, including those who actually received other therapy. A crude tox_stop_8wk rate among TXR1i-treated patients is biased if their germline DLR1 status or clinical makeup differs from the whole target population. Toxicity under TXR1i probably depends on DLR1 metabolizer status: compute an activity score as the sum of the two haplotype activity values from dlr1_allele_table instead of treating each star allele as its own category; tabulate tox_stop_8wk by activity score under TXR1i; check dlr1_call_confidence and ancestry_group. Estimate the risk by standardizing (g-computation or IPW) over the whole target population's covariates, activity score included, and handle low-confidence diplotype calls with a sensitivity analysis or multiple imputation.

sl-dev-v2-local-d92b0aef00c9.label: PLAN
sl-dev-v2-local-d92b0aef00c9.text: PLAN: Estimand = within SV-driven TXR1 target population (analysis_set==1, time zero aligned), standardized marginal risk difference in week-16 benefit (TXR1i vs SYS) under hypothetical full assessment, plus marginal 8-week tox risk under TXR1i standardized over the whole target population; net = RD - 0.35*tox. Target definition: P2T topology, excluding artifact-prone calls (low MAPQ/segdup without ASE/phase support), with purity/copy-adjusted alt fraction and haplotype-consistent ASE/phase; sensitivity under stricter/looser definitions. Method: AIPW / g-computation with logistic outcome models on baseline covariates (ecog, burden, prior lines, resistance, lineage, site, period, age, sex), missingness handled by MAR outcome modelling among assessed plus IPCW-AIPW; toxicity via g-computation including DLR1 activity score. Checks: overlap/ESS/SMD, positivity by site/period, assessed16 patterns, expression batch effects, DLR1 confidence, bootstrap CIs. Change method if positivity fails (report overlap region), if missingness depends on tox (then include post-treatment tox in missingness model only), or if target definition is unstable.

sl-dev-v2-local-a9892a42fb79.label: PLAN
sl-dev-v2-local-a9892a42fb79.text: PLAN: Target = patients in analysis_set==1 whose tumor has a credible SV-driven TXR1 activation: long-read P2T promoter-facing junction that is not a mapping artifact (segdup/low complexity/high homology/low MAPQ), with supporting allele-specific expression on the breakpoint haplotype and TXR1 expression elevated beyond lineage/purity expectation; copy gain alone or INV/D2T are not SV-driven activation. Estimand 1: marginal risk difference in week-16 benefit (TXR1i vs SYS) if all were assessed, estimated by doubly robust AIPW combining treatment propensity (age, sex, site, period, ecog, burden, prior lines/resistance, lineage) and missingness (assessed16) model on same covariates plus treatment; compare with g-computation and complete-case. Estimand 2: standardized 8-week toxicity risk under TXR1i in target (g-formula incl. DLR1 activity score from star alleles). Checks: overlap of propensity, sensitivity to target definition thresholds, missingness predictors, DLR1 call confidence, expression batch, time-zero set. Change method if target definition is driven by artifacts, positivity fails, or results swing widely across reasonable definitions.

sl-dev-v2-local-cd42e06fc3ab.reason: This fixes the core estimator for t; using the naive formula changes the reported time by a large factor that depends on each haplotype's ancestry fraction.
sl-dev-v2-local-cd42e06fc3ab.text: Do not estimate the admixture time as t = 1/(mean tract length). Recombination between two segments of the same ancestry is invisible, so under a single pulse t generations ago with ancestry-A fraction m, A tracts are exponential with rate t*(1-m) per Morgan and B tracts with rate t*m per Morgan. The naive estimator is off by a factor 1/(1-m) (or 1/m) and is badly wrong when m is far from 0.5. Estimate t jointly instead, for example t = S / (2*m*(1-m)*L), where S is the number of observed ancestry switches and L is the total called span in Morgans, or equivalently t = 1/(mean_A_length*(1-m)). As a check, estimate t separately from the A tracts (rate t*(1-m)) and from the B tracts (rate t*m) of the same haplotype; the two should agree with each other, while the naive 1/mean will not.

sl-dev-v2-local-ade096975d65.reason: With one individual, a large share of tracts touch a chromosome end, so how edges are handled moves t materially.
sl-dev-v2-local-ade096975d65.text: Tracts that touch the start or end of a chromosome, or the edge of the called span, are censored: their observed length is shorter than their true length. Treating them as complete tracts shortens the mean and inflates t. Per chromosome and haplotype, count the segments that begin at the first called coordinate or end at the last, see what share of the span they hold, and compare boundary with interior tract lengths. Use the censored exponential estimator: rate = (number of uncensored tract ends, that is observed ancestry switches) / (total Morgan span of all tracts of that ancestry, censored ones included). Equivalently, count switches as events and total span as exposure; chromosome ends are not switches.

sl-dev-v2-local-a629cce5274d.reason: The task asks for the fraction 'across the called tract span'; the choice of denominator directly sets both fractions and feeds into t.
sl-dev-v2-local-a629cce5274d.text: The ancestry-A fraction must be weighted by genetic length (Morgans) over the span actually called. It is not a count of segments, and the denominator is not physical position or the whole chromosome length. The called span can be shorter than the chromosome lengths given in map_info.tsv, and dividing by chromosome length deflates both fractions. For each haplotype, sum segment lengths per chromosome and compare with length_morgan in map_info.tsv to quantify uncalled flanks and interior gaps, and check that both haplotypes cover the same span. Use the sum of retained, called segment lengths in Morgans per haplotype as the denominator, and use that same span as the exposure in the rate estimate for t.

sl-dev-v2-local-48a676aefe54.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-dev-v2-local-48a676aefe54.text: WARNING SIGN: 252 of 1036 analysis-set P2T calls have segmental_dup_overlap=1 with mapq_median<45 (mean homology 24bp, low_complexity 0.70); despite ASE/phase looking similar, crude TXR1i benefit in them is 4.0% vs 17.8% SYS, unlike clean P2T (32.3% vs 17.2%). MEANS: these are likely mis-mapping artifacts, not SV-driven. ACTION: excluded from primary target population; sensitivity including them reported.

sl-dev-v2-local-7c2bbc3a68d6.reason: Each spurious short segment adds two switches, so artefact filtering can change t substantially; the data carry quality columns meant for this check.
sl-dev-v2-local-7c2bbc3a68d6.text: Very short segments produced by local-ancestry inference error (low posterior, repeats or low-complexity regions) add fake ancestry switches and inflate t. Tabulate segment length against the posterior and low_complexity_frac columns and look for an excess of segments below roughly 1-2 cM concentrated at low posterior or high low_complexity_frac. If present, drop segments that fail a posterior threshold (for example below 0.9) or have high low_complexity_frac (for example above 0.5), remove their span from the denominator instead of counting them as switches, and report how sensitive t is to the chosen threshold.

sl-dev-v2-local-9569d42d8a46.reason: This is the necessary follow-up to segment filtering; skipping it makes the switch count and t wrong.
sl-dev-v2-local-9569d42d8a46.text: After filtering, or across uncalled gaps, two adjacent segments of the same ancestry on the same chromosome and haplotype are one tract, not two tracts separated by a switch. Leaving them unmerged roughly doubles the inferred switch rate. Scan each chromosome and haplotype for consecutive rows with the same ancestry label and for same-ancestry pairs flanking a dropped or uncalled interval. Merge them into one tract, summing their lengths and excluding the uncalled interval from the span, before any mean-length or likelihood calculation.

sl-dev-v2-local-402b6f3f0574.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-dev-v2-local-402b6f3f0574.text: WARNING SIGN: week-16 non-assessment is driven by tox_stop_8wk (assessed 16-19% if tox=1 vs 88-89% if tox=0), and TXR1i tox rate is ~31% vs ~9% SYS in P2T. MEANS: complete-case benefit is biased; MAR must condition on post-baseline tox. ACTION: sequential g-computation/AIPW: outcome model among assessed given arm, baseline X and tox, integrated over tox|arm,X; tox never used in propensity model or cohort restriction.

sl-dev-v2-local-d4d6e095a26f.reason: Phase errors within a chromosome corrupt both the per-parent fractions and the per-parent times, which are exactly the quantities asked for.
sl-dev-v2-local-d4d6e095a26f.text: A phasing switch error inside a chromosome looks like a real ancestry switch. Its signature is two coincident, opposite breakpoints: h1 and h2 switch at the same Morgan coordinate in opposite directions (A-to-B on one, B-to-A on the other). This inflates the switch count on both haplotypes, biases t upward and mixes the two parents' ancestry fractions. List breakpoint coordinates for h1 and h2 per chromosome and flag such coincident opposite switches. If found, treat it as a phase error, flip the haplotype assignment downstream of that point to restore the longer tracts, and recompute. If the pattern is frequent, prefer an estimator of parental fractions and times that does not depend on phase.

sl-dev-v2-local-7a56028b7a33.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-dev-v2-local-7a56028b7a33.text: WARNING SIGN: under TXR1i, tox_stop_8wk is ~68-92% when DLR1 activity score <=1.0 vs ~21% at >=1.5; SYS ~10% regardless. MEANS: toxicity risk must be standardized over activity score distribution of target population. ACTION: toxicity g-computation includes activity score as categorical.

sl-dev-v2-local-f0c93282eb31.reason: Whether h1/h2 map to the same parent across chromosomes decides how segments are pooled into parent1 and parent2, which changes all four reported numbers.
sl-dev-v2-local-f0c93282eb31.text: Haplotype labels h1 and h2 may be assigned independently per chromosome, so h1 need not be the same parent on every chromosome. Pooling chromosomes under mislabelled haplotypes pulls both parental A-fractions toward the genome-wide mean, so the parental difference is understated and the times are distorted. Compute the per-chromosome A-fraction of h1 minus h2 and check whether the sign is consistent across chromosomes; inconsistent signs with large magnitudes point to label swapping, a consistent sign supports genome-wide-consistent labels. If labels must be resolved per chromosome (for example by maximising the between-haplotype separation in A-fraction), say that this choice biases the estimated difference upward, and cross-check with an unphased, homozygosity-based estimate of the two parental fractions.

sl-dev-v2-local-5f6ec948e6b9.reason: A label swap or a pooled time would make every answer key wrong even if the underlying estimates are sound.
sl-dev-v2-local-5f6ec948e6b9.text: Fit the A-fraction and t independently for each haplotype. Do not force the two haplotypes to share one admixture time or pool their tracts into one likelihood, because the task asks for the two parental histories separately and they may genuinely differ. Assign the parent1/parent2 labels only after all QC and filtering is settled: filtering changes each haplotype's A-fraction, so labelling early can swap the labels. Recompute the A-fractions after every filtering decision, check whether the ordering ever changes, and report the gap between the two fractions so that a near-tie is visible.

sl-dev-v2-local-aaebd71c4325.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-dev-v2-local-aaebd71c4325.text: WARNING SIGN: D2T/INV junction cases (n=137) have high TXR1 expression, ASE and phase similar to P2T but crude TXR1i benefit 5.3% vs SYS 18.4%. MEANS: non-promoter-facing junctions are not target-mediated activation; expression/ASE alone would misclassify. ACTION: excluded from target.

sl-dev-v2-local-2c0e68cd704b.reason: An unstated off-by-one in the generation count is a silent error when t is small; the team should pick the convention deliberately and report it.
sl-dev-v2-local-2c0e68cd704b.text: The generation convention is ambiguous and can shift t by a whole generation. A transmitted haplotype has passed through one meiosis per generation since the pulse, including the meiosis that produced the focal individual, so a recombination rate per Morgan measures the number of meioses, which is not necessarily what is meant by generations. State explicitly which convention is used. The recommended convention is the one in which A tracts are exponential with rate t*(1-m), with t the generations since the admixture pulse for that parental haplotype; say so in the reasoning so the number can be interpreted.

sl-dev-v2-local-0d755f73e670.reason: It determines which estimator to report and how to express uncertainty, and the grading weighs the quality of reasoning as well as the number.
sl-dev-v2-local-0d755f73e670.text: One individual's genome gives few tracts, so the time estimate has a large variance and a known downward bias, and for very recent admixture tract lengths are not truly exponential or independent. Count the uncensored tracts per haplotype. If there are fewer than about 20, give a confidence interval for the rate (a Poisson interval on the switch count divided by the exposure in Morgans) and derive t three ways, from the A tracts, from the B tracts and from the pooled switch rate, to see whether they agree. Report t from the pooled switch-rate estimator, not from one ancestry's mean length, state the interval, and do not round the point estimate to a precision the data cannot support.

sl-dev-v2-local-61294b0648aa.label: PLAN
sl-dev-v2-local-61294b0648aa.text: PLAN: Estimate per-haplotype ancestry-A fraction (Morgan-weighted over called span, gaps excluded) and t via pooled censored switch-rate estimator t = S/(2 m (1-m) L) with S = interior ancestry switches between adjacent called segments, L = called span; convention: A tracts exponential with rate t(1-m). Checks: low-posterior/low-complexity short segments (drop if posterior<0.9 or lcf>0.5, remove span, merge flanks), same-ancestry flanks across gaps merged, chromosome ends censored not switches, coincident opposite breakpoints h1/h2 (phase errors), per-chrom sign of h1-h2 A fraction (label swapping), t from A tracts vs B tracts vs pooled, Poisson CI, threshold sensitivity, unphased cross-check. Change method if per-chrom signs inconsistent (resolve labels per chrom) or coincident switches indicate phase errors.

sl-dev-v2-local-0bfd6b986a40.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-dev-v2-local-0bfd6b986a40.text: WARNING SIGN: in primary target (n=666), g-computation benefit RD 18.1pp vs AIPW 14.0pp; control-arm ESS 104 of 206, max IPW 29, max weighted SMD 0.128 (siteS4, P3). MEANS: some model dependence and moderate overlap; net utility (2.5 to 6.4pp) is near zero so sign is sensitive. ACTION: kept AIPW as primary, adding flexible terms and bootstrap to quantify uncertainty; no trimming.

sl-dev-v2-local-fad50c639de9.label: PLAN
sl-dev-v2-local-fad50c639de9.text: PLAN: Estimate per-parental-haplotype ancestry-A fraction (A length / called length) and pulse time t via the two-state Markov (Gravel) tract model: A tracts end at rate t(1-m), B at rate t*m, so MLE t = switches / (L_A*(1-m) + L_B*m). Checks: mask low-posterior/high low-complexity segments (posterior 0.62, lcf 0.92) and merge identical flanks; handle uncalled gaps (exclude from span, sensitivity on counting switches across gaps); check that h1/h2 labels are phased consistently across chromosomes (phase is arbitrary between chromosomes) by examining per-chromosome tract density and A fraction and choosing the chromosome-to-parent assignment; compare to chromosome-end censoring. Change method if masking or phase assignment changes estimates materially.

sl-dev-v2-local-c4f1bef7d63f.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-dev-v2-local-c4f1bef7d63f.text: WARNING SIGN: AIPW benefit RD point 14.0pp but bootstrap median 19.8pp (95% 3.7-34.2) while g-computation is 18.1pp (bootstrap 9.1-32.0); the AIPW missingness term uses weights up to 1/(P(A)*P(R)) with P(assessed|tox=1) ~0.17, so it is unstable. sl-dev-v2-local-dc901a4632b3.text: gb01 result (team-a): target = analysis_set P2T calls excluding segdup+MAPQ<45 artifacts and requiring ASE>0.62 and phase>0.6 (n=666, 460 TXR1i). Sequential g-computation (MAR given arm, baseline X, tox_stop_8wk) gives week-16 benefit RD 18.1pp, standardized TXR1i 8-week tox 33.5pp (DLR1 activity score in model), net utility 6.4pp, therapy code 1; AIPW gives 14.0/32.9/2.5.

sl-dev-v2-local-aae27e662e16.text: WARNING SIGN: in the core target (n=475), tox_stop_8wk strongly predicts a missing week-16 assessment (logit coef -4.1), and TXR1i raises toxicity via DLR1 activity (T x DLR1 activity score coef -1.5). sl-dev-v2-local-9a2e57e5fbca.text: WARNING SIGN: 8 segments of exactly 0.03 M with posterior 0.62 and low_complexity_frac 0.92 (one per chrom per haplotype, at identical coordinates on h1 and h2 with opposite ancestry), every other segment has posterior 0.985/lcf 0.08; they add 16 fake switches (36->28 on h1, 22->14 on h2) and raise t from ~5.3 to 6.7 and ~2.6 to 4.0 under the given labels. MEANS: LAI artefacts that also mimic coincident opposite phase breakpoints. ACTION: dropped them (posterior<0.9 or lcf>0.5), removed their span from exposure, merged same-ancestry flanks; result identical for any posterior threshold 0.7-0.95.

sl-dev-v2-local-cee49fca8dd9.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-dev-v2-local-cee49fca8dd9.text: WARNING SIGN: per-chromosome A-fraction h1 minus h2 is +0.23, +0.46, -0.67, +0.40 on chr1-4; chr3 has the opposite sign with the largest magnitude; pooled-as-given fractions 0.565/0.482 are much closer than the unphased AA/AB/BB-based solution 0.337/0.713. MEANS: haplotype labels are not consistent across chromosomes (chr3 swapped), pooling under given labels shrinks the parental difference and mixes switch counts. ACTION: changed method: resolve h1/h2 labels per chromosome (swap chr3) and recompute fractions and t per parent; cross-checked against the unphased estimate.

sl-dev-v2-local-d378abf9a4b0.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-dev-v2-local-d378abf9a4b0.text: WARNING SIGN: called span is 2.62-2.98 M per chromosome vs map lengths 2.8-3.1 M (flanks of 0.02-0.18 M uncalled) and there are 1-2 interior gaps of 0.02-0.04 M per chromosome-haplotype, with different gap positions on h1 and h2. MEANS: denominator must be the called span not chromosome length; gaps between different ancestries still imply a switch. ACTION: used summed called segment lengths as denominator/exposure; counted ancestry changes across gaps as switches; sensitivity with gap span split into flanks changes t by <2%.

sl-dev-v2-local-19f35ba9a43d.label: RESULT
sl-dev-v2-local-19f35ba9a43d.text: Result: in the core SV-activated target (clean P2T, ASE>=0.68, phase>=0.75, copy<=3.6, alt fraction>=0.1; n=475) the AIPW week-16 benefit RD for TXR1i vs SYS is 33.5pp (bootstrap 95% CI 22.9-42.8), the standardized 8-week toxicity risk under TXR1i is 32.8pp (28.4-37.1), and net utility is 22.0pp (11.1-30.4). Using all P2T calls instead shrinks the RD to about 12pp, so the net utility falls to about 0.

sl-dev-v2-local-a063aff020a3.text: gb02 result: after dropping 8 artefact segments (posterior 0.62, lcf 0.92), merging same-ancestry flanks and swapping chr3 haplotype labels (only configuration of 8 giving a consistent h1-h2 sign on all chromosomes, also the max-separation one), parent1 (lower A) has A fraction 0.301 over 10.87 M with 16 switches, t = S/(2m(1-m)L) = 3.50 (95% Poisson CI 2.0-5.7; A-tract 3.06, B-tract 3.93); parent2 has A fraction 0.747 over 10.83 M with 26 switches, t = 6.34 (CI 4.1-9.3). Check whether the h1 gap and the h2 gap near 1.48-1.51 M on chr1 overlap in coordinates, and tabulate for all 12 gaps whether a gap on one haplotype overlaps a gap or breakpoint on the other. sl-dev-v2-local-d0b74e05fbbe.reason: question from the director challenging the answer both teams agreed on
sl-dev-v2-local-d0b74e05fbbe.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: You said your t convention may differ from another by about 1 generation, and your exposure excludes gap length while each gap still contributes a switch. Recompute t for each parent (a) with gap length added back to the exposure, (b) with the artefact span kept and assigned flank ancestry, and (c) from A tracts alone and from B tracts alone using map_info chromosome ends to decide which boundary tracts are censored. Do the A-tract and B-tract estimates agree within their intervals, and does any of these change the t you report or the convention you state?

sl-dev-v2-local-77b21bc5b306.label: REPLY low-confidence DLR1 calls
sl-dev-v2-local-77b21bc5b306.text: REPLY on low-confidence DLR1 calls: 44 of 666 target cases (6.6%, 36 below 0.90) have dlr1_call_confidence<0.95 and are enriched in ancestry group G3; their activity scores pile up at 1.0 while their observed TXR1i 8-week toxicity at score 1.0 is about 0.17 versus 0.88-1.00 for high-confidence cases with score<=1.0, so the summed-haplotype activity score is unreliable for them and attenuates the activity-toxicity gradient used to standardize toxicity risk.

sl-dev-v2-local-9d3fba6f5b64.label: REPLY DLR1 confidence effect on estimates
sl-dev-v2-local-9d3fba6f5b64.text: REPLY on how the DLR1 confidence check changed the method: standardized 8-week TXR1i toxicity in the SV-driven target moves from 33.47pp with activity scores as called, to 34.93pp with 20-draw multiple imputation of activity for low-confidence calls from the ancestry-matched high-confidence distribution, to 36.59pp if low-confidence cases are dropped (which narrows the estimand); week-16 benefit risk difference moves 18.11 to 16.88; net clinical utility stays positive in all three (6.40, 4.65, 4.12) so therapy_class_code remains 1, and the primary estimate was revised to the imputation version (benefit 16.88pp, toxicity 34.93pp, net 4.65pp).

sl-dev-v2-local-d7d0f7e242ae.label: REPLY target CCF
sl-dev-v2-local-d7d0f7e242ae.text: REPLY (target definition): replacing the raw alt-molecule-fraction cut-off with a purity- and copy-corrected clonality estimate CCF=AF*(purity*copy+2*(1-purity))/purity, thresholded at 0.55 where its distribution is bimodal, justifies the target from molecular data alone; it moves only 6 of 481 patients and changes the benefit RD by 0.1pp, while dropping the clonality/copy requirement altogether (haplotype-link only, n=604) lowers the RD to 25.8pp.

sl-dev-v2-local-9715a53c6361.label: REPLY confounders
sl-dev-v2-local-9715a53c6361.text: REPLY (confounding and positivity): treatment positivity holds in all 12 site-by-calendar-period cells of the gb01 target (P(TXR1i) 0.65-0.85), but DLR1 activity score (weighted SMD 0.55) and tumour purity (-0.17) were imbalanced because they were missing from the propensity model; adding them lowers the AIPW week-16 benefit RD from 33.5pp to 29.1pp.

sl-dev-v2-local-7c66a27b9b12.label: REPLY
sl-dev-v2-local-7c66a27b9b12.text: gb02 reply on filtering/threshold sensitivity: the 8 dropped segments are all exactly 0.03 M with posterior 0.62 and low_complexity_frac 0.92 (all other segments 0.985/0.08); results are identical for any posterior cutoff in 0.7-0.95, while keeping them (cutoff<=0.62) inflates t from 3.4/6.2 to 5.1/8.0 via 16 fake switches. Filtering kept, method unchanged.

sl-dev-v2-local-417fd1f9b723.label: REPLY weight stability
sl-dev-v2-local-417fd1f9b723.text: REPLY (weights): in the gb01 target the combined treatment-by-assessment weights are stable (effective sample size 141 of 238 TXR1i and 56 of 107 comparator, maximum weight 31, only 6 patients at the 0.05 assessment floor) and AIPW, IPW and outcome-model standardization agree within about 2pp, so AIPW remains the primary estimator.

sl-dev-v2-local-e1fe947028d2.label: REPLY
sl-dev-v2-local-e1fe947028d2.text: gb02 reply on denominators: A-fraction uses called tract Morgans only (low-A 10.866 M, high-A 10.834 M), giving 0.301 and 0.747. But every interior gap in the data sits at an ancestry switch, so the breakpoint lies inside the gap and the gap belongs in the switch-rate exposure. Using the first-to-last called span (11.150 M) changes t from 3.50/6.34 to 3.41/6.16. This is a revision (~3%, not the <2% stated before).

sl-dev-v2-local-cf53b390ca77.label: REPLY toxicity categorical
sl-dev-v2-local-cf53b390ca77.text: REPLY (toxicity coding): observed 8-week TXR1i toxicity by DLR1 activity score is 100, 90, 59, 22, 22 percent at scores 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, which a linear term cannot fit; recoding the score as categorical and standardizing over the whole target raises the TXR1i toxicity risk from 32.8pp to 33.5pp, giving net utility 29.14-0.35*33.53=17.4pp and therapy_class_code 1.

sl-dev-v2-local-d191ae29040c.label: REPLY
sl-dev-v2-local-d191ae29040c.text: gb02 reply on t estimators: with gap-inclusive exposure, low-A parent t pooled 3.41, from A tracts 2.99, from B tracts 3.83; high-A parent pooled 6.16, A 6.27, B 5.88. The A and B estimates agree within Poisson error (S=16 and 26 switches). Pooled censored switch-rate estimator reported; naive 1/mean length (1.8/2.8) rejected.

sl-dev-v2-local-64a7c7cbb08a.label: REPLY
sl-dev-v2-local-64a7c7cbb08a.text: gb02 reply on labels/phasing: joint Markov (censored exponential) likelihood over all 8 per-chromosome h1/h2 configurations, fitting m and t per parent, prefers swapping chr3 (negLL 13.47 vs next best 16.93, same parameter count), so the chr3 swap is supported by both tract lengths and fractions, not only separation. Labels were assigned after filtering: parent1 = low-A (0.301), parent2 = high-A (0.747).

sl-dev-v2-local-1778233cace6.label: REPLY
sl-dev-v2-local-1778233cace6.text: gb02 reply on generation convention: t is reported as the rate parameter of the single-pulse model (A tracts exponential with rate t(1-m), B with rate t*m per Morgan), i.e. meioses along the transmitted lineage since the pulse, which equals the parent's generation number after the pulse. A convention counting the unrecombined source generation would add 1; I did not apply that shift.

sl-dev-v2-local-a9723acba3df.label: REPLY
sl-dev-v2-local-a9723acba3df.text: Q1: Does switch density alone (no A fraction) place chr3 h2 with h1 of the other chromosomes? Check: q.py: per chromosome-haplotype switch densities, Poisson switch-density-only log-likelihood for every assignment vs the full Markov likelihood and an A-fraction-only term. Finding: Density alone weakly prefers no flip (LL -11.87 vs -13.05; -14.73 vs -15.34 after the chr1 fix), with chr3 h1 at 2.03/M vs h2 at 1.36/M. The signal is about 1 log unit, and the expected density 2tm(1-m) itself depends on m. The A-fraction signal dominates, and the full likelihood prefers the chr3 flip. Changes method: no.

sl-dev-v2-local-36532ceedbb9.label: REPLY
sl-dev-v2-local-36532ceedbb9.text: Q2: Do the chr1 gaps overlap, and how do overlaps across all 12 gaps compare with chance (using gap width)? Check: q2.py: overlap table for all 12 gaps against gaps and breakpoints on the other haplotype; expected chance overlaps from event density times (gap width + mean other width). Finding: The chr1 h1 gap (1.4788-1.5037, A->B) overlaps the h2 gap (1.4854-1.5132, B->A); it is the only overlap among the 12 gaps. Expected chance overlaps: 0.48 pairs of any kind, and 0.14 for an opposite-direction gap-on-gap pair (P about 0.13), not 0.7. The correction removes 2 switches and leaves the likelihood unchanged or slightly better (+0.1). chr1 was corrected. Changes method: YES.

sl-dev-v2-local-9c5cc84aaa56.label: REPLY
sl-dev-v2-local-9c5cc84aaa56.text: Q3: t with gap length in the exposure, with the artifact span kept, and from A and B tracts separately with censoring Check: q34.py: variants (a), (b) and (c) for both parents, with and without the chr1 fix. Finding: (a) 4.34/6.15, (b) 4.41/6.25 vs the reported 4.43/6.27. (c) Parent1 tA=3.9 and tB=4.9; parent2 6.3 and 6.3. These agree within their intervals; the check is weak because L_A(1-m)=L_B*m. The reported t and the convention t = switches per M / (2m(1-m)) are unchanged. Changes method: no.

sl-dev-v2-local-5b783db9123c.label: REPLY
sl-dev-v2-local-5b783db9123c.text: Q4: Is the best-of-8 dLL for the chr3 flip in the far tail of a null with the same selection? Check: q4.py: 5000 simulations under the labels-as-given fit with best-of-8 selection. Finding: Observed dLL 4.62 vs null 99% quantile 4.38, P=0.008. With the chr1 fix, 7.11 vs 5.20, P=0.002. The flip is kept. Changes method: no.

sl-dev-v2-local-e18a5b81666a.label: REFEREE TEST
sl-dev-v2-local-e18a5b81666a.text: gb01 referee: X's target (n=481) is a strict subset of Y's (n=666); the 185 Y-only P2T cases are mostly high local copy (median 5.3) with subclonal junction (purity/copy-corrected CCF median 0.30). Adjusted g-computation (MAR given covariates, arm, 8-wk tox) gives TXR1i benefit RD +24.7pp (boot CI 13-35) in the 481 core vs -10.4pp (CI -18 to +7) in the 185 disputed cases, and their TXR1 expression excess over NONE cases is about half the core's and tracks CCF. So the disputed cases do not behave as target-mediated activation; X's narrower target was supported. Code: runs/dev-v2-local/gb01/referee/work/test1.py, test2.py.

sl-dev-v2-local-c2451e8acc6b.label: REFEREE TEST
sl-dev-v2-local-c2451e8acc6b.text: In gb02 (local-ancestry tracts), the overlapping opposite-direction gaps on chr1 near 1.49 M do not show a phase-switch error. Under a no-phase-error null (independent Markov pulse haplotypes, m/t = 0.301/3.41 and 0.747/6.16, observed gap rate and widths, 20000 simulations), P(opposite switches within 0.008 M) = 0.26 and P(an overlapping opposite gap pair) = 0.087. So the chr1 swap is not supported, and the uncorrected answer stands: about 0.301/t 3.41 and 0.747/t 6.16, after masking the 8 low-posterior artefacts and flipping chr3.
